brief.outcome: Bring the share of open invoices that are past due at a marketing agency (55 retainer clients, monthly invoices on 30-day terms in FreshBooks) from about 40% to under 15% within three months, without losing clients.

ambition.goal_beyond: Retainer clients pay on time as a habit, so the agency's cash is steady and the owner stops chasing by hand
rungs: Chase the invoices that are overdue now with approved reminders
Find why invoices are late (invoice timing, wrong contact, payment friction, a few chronic accounts, disputes) and fix the process with a reminder schedule before and after the due date
Keep it true: a weekly aging check that flags clients starting to slip before they reach 30 days late
ambition.judge: FreshBooks' own aging report (share of open invoices past due, and days to pay by invoice month) and the bank deposits that match paid invoices, read weekly for the three months

brief.deliverable: A working collections routine in FreshBooks: current overdue invoices chased with approved emails, a reminder schedule switched on with approval, an escalation policy the owner has approved, and a weekly aging check with an honest readout at three months

research.approach: Practitioners treat late payment as a process problem before a client problem. They start from the aging report and the raw invoice and payment history, check the report is true (payments recorded, invoices accurate and sent to the right contact), then split overdue invoices by age and by client to see whether lateness is a few chronic accounts, a general habit or a system gap. The fix is a written cadence: a courtesy note before the due date, a friendly reminder shortly after, firmer notes with a payment link in each message, a phone call at the middle stage, and a decision at 60 days (payment plan, pause, agency or write-off) made by a named person. They invoice promptly and make paying easy, because delays start before the reminders. Results are read as days-to-pay and aging buckets weekly, with the relationship protected by sending firm messages only after a person has looked at disputes or hardship.

sources.title: Ramp: accounts receivable management
sources.note: Invoice on the day of delivery with clear payment instructions and due date; remind about a week before due, on the due date and shortly after, with a payment link in each; review aging monthly in buckets (current, 1-30, 31-60, 61-90, 90+); tiered escalation by days past due.

sources.title: Ramp: days sales outstanding
sources.note: DSO is receivables divided by credit sales times days in the period. To reduce it: invoice faster, remind at the halfway point and a few days before due, review customers whose habits have slipped, make paying simple (bank transfer, card, portal).

sources.title: FreshBooks Help: late payment fees and reminders
sources.note: Accessed 2026-11-03. Up to three automatic reminders per client, before or after the due date, set per client or for all new invoices; one-time reminders can be sent manually. Late fees are optional and apply to new invoices. Other pages disagree on whether turning reminders on reaches existing invoices, so test on one client first.

sources.title: Beancount.io: unpaid invoices dunning cadence guide
sources.note: Accessed 2026-11-03; the page shows no date. Cadence of courtesy note before due, friendly at day 7, firmer with a call at day 15, formal notice at day 30, final at day 45, decision at day 60; put a payment link at the top; address a decision-maker; log every contact. Vendor-style blog, so treat day counts as one example to test.

steps.name: Design the reminder cadence and escalation
steps.why: A written schedule with tone per stage and a decision at 60 days replaces chasing when someone remembers.

steps.name: Draft the reminders for current overdue invoices, client by client
steps.why: One message per client, in the agency's voice, with a payment link and the invoice, and no firm tone for disputes.

steps.name: Read aging and days-to-pay weekly

pitfalls.text: Chasing invoices that were already paid but not recorded, or that are in dispute.
Judging success only by the overdue share, which falls slowly when old invoices stay open; days-to-pay on new invoices shows the change sooner.
Sending the same firm message to every client, including long-standing retainers who forgot.
Turning on automatic reminders for all clients at once without testing what they send and to whom.
Invoicing late, so terms start late and the reminders cannot fix it.

stages.name: Pin down the late-payment problem
stages.goal: Turn the owner's words into a measured problem, a target, limits and the data we can reach. Writes BRIEF.md.

stages.name: Gather invoice and payment history
stages.goal: Pull invoices, payments, the aging report, client contacts and reminder settings for the last 12 months into one CSV set.

checks.name: Open invoice totals in the dataset match the FreshBooks aging report total within 1%
States the past-due share both by number of invoices and by value, so the 40% is pinned to one definition
Any export not provided is listed with what it would unlock

stages.name: Check the aging report is true
stages.goal: Find invoices that look overdue but are paid but unrecorded, duplicated, disputed, credited, or sent to a wrong or bouncing contact, before anyone is chased.

outputs.name: Hold list for invoices not to chase yet

checks.name: Each overdue invoice is compared with bank deposits for the same amount and client, or the check is marked limited
Overdue invoices with no view, a bounce or a different payer contact are listed
Ends with CHECKED, LIMITED or UNRELIABLE and the corrected past-due share

stages.name: Find why invoices are paid late
stages.goal: Split overdue invoices by age bucket, client and cause; separate chronic accounts from one-offs and process gaps from client behaviour. Keep competing explanations.

checks.name: Every hypothesis is SUPPORTED, REFUTED or UNKNOWN, with the rows it rests on
A client-level finding is made only with at least 3 invoices for that client, otherwise marked low-confidence
Shares are given by value as well as by count
Each main finding names a competing explanation

stages.name: Rank the collection actions
stages.goal: Turn supported findings into ranked cards: which clients to call, the reminder schedule, payment-method fixes, invoice timing, escalation steps at 60 days, payment plans.

checks.name: Every card cites the finding it rests on
Every card has expected effect on the past-due share, effort, confidence, risk to the client relationship and how it will be measured
No card sends anything without the owner's approval or adds a late fee without the owner's choice

stages.name: The owner chooses
stages.goal: The owner picks card IDs and decides the 60-day rule (payment plan, pause, agency or write-off). Ask for the reason when they pass over a top card; record it.

checks.name: Chosen and passed-over cards are in decisions.jsonl
A reason is recorded wherever a top card was passed over
The owner's rule for the 60-day case is recorded in the owner's words

stages.name: Draft the reminders and the schedule
stages.goal: Draft one reminder per overdue client (tone by days late, payment link, invoice attached, skipping the hold list), plus the automatic reminder schedule and the escalation policy for the owner.

checks.name: No draft is written for an invoice on the hold list, and disputes get a question, not a demand
Every draft states the correct invoice number, amount, due date and days late, checked against the dataset
Tone matches the days-late stage and the client's history, and every draft has a payment link or clear pay instruction
All drafts are saved as drafts; nothing is sent

stages.name: Send the approved reminders
stages.goal: Register the baseline, then send each reminder only after the owner approves that email. Record what was sent, to whom and when.

checks.name: Every email in the log has the owner's yes recorded before it was sent
The baseline past-due share and the send dates are in experiments.jsonl before the first send
Each contact is logged with date, channel, person and any promise

stages.name: Switch on automatic reminders and payment options
stages.goal: Switch on the approved reminder schedule on one client first, check what it sends and to whom, then roll out to the rest and add the approved payment methods, one change at a time with the owner's yes.

checks.name: One client is switched on first and the reminder that goes out is read back for wording, recipient and timing
Each setting read back from FreshBooks matches what was approved
Rollout to the other clients is in two groups at least 2 weeks apart, so the second group is a control for the first

stages.optional_when: No schedule or payment-method card was chosen.

stages.name: Read aging and days-to-pay weekly
stages.goal: Each week read the past-due share, the aging buckets, days-to-pay on invoices issued after the change, and the guardrails, and flag clients who are starting to slip.

Days-to-pay for invoices issued after the change are compared with invoices issued in the same number of months before
Clients lost, complaints and disputes raised are each checked
A process claim needs at least two monthly invoicing cycles (about 110 invoices) after the change; one cycle is a signal only

stages.name: Keep what we learned
stages.goal: Close each experiment, save collection rules with their scope, and plan the next round.

checks.name: Every registered experiment is closed in experiments.jsonl with a verdict

hypotheses.statement: Some 'overdue' invoices have already been paid but not recorded.
hypotheses.test: Match overdue invoices with bank deposits by amount, client and date.
hypotheses.confirm_if: At least 5% of overdue value matches a deposit.

hypotheses.statement: No consistent reminders: invoices with no reminder sent are paid later.
hypotheses.test: Days late for invoices with a reminder in the sent history versus none; settings screenshot.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Median days late is at least 14 days longer where no reminder was sent, or automatic reminders are off.
hypotheses.refute_if: Days late are similar with and without a reminder.

hypotheses.statement: Lateness is concentrated in a few chronic clients.
hypotheses.test: Overdue value and days late by client; top 10 share.
hypotheses.confirm_if: The top 10 clients hold 60% or more of overdue value.
hypotheses.refute_if: Overdue value is spread over more than 30 clients, none above 5%.

hypotheses.statement: A large part of the overdue balance is over 90 days and probably disputed or uncollectable.
hypotheses.test: Share of overdue value over 90 days; whether those clients are still active.
hypotheses.confirm_if: More than 25% of overdue value is over 90 days.

hypotheses.statement: Invoices go out late or to the wrong contact, so terms start late.
hypotheses.test: Days between service period start and issue date; views, bounces and contact mismatches.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Median issue date is more than 5 days after the period start, or more than 10% of overdue invoices were never viewed or bounced.
hypotheses.refute_if: Invoices go out within 2 days and nearly all are viewed.

hypotheses.statement: It is hard to pay: no online payment option or no payment link.
hypotheses.test: Payment methods switched on; share of paid invoices paid online.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Online payment is off, or under 20% of paid invoices were paid online.
hypotheses.refute_if: Online payment is on and over 50% of paid invoices are paid that way.

hypotheses.statement: In practice clients pay on 45 to 60 days, not 30.
hypotheses.test: Median days to pay for invoices paid in the last 6 months.

hypotheses.statement: The most overdue clients are also the ones the agency can least afford to upset.
hypotheses.test: Retainer value and tenure of the overdue clients compared with the book.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Five or more overdue clients are in the top fifth of retainers by value.
hypotheses.refute_if: Overdue clients are mostly small retainers.

measurement.window: Twelve weeks, read weekly; days-to-pay for invoices issued after the change compared with the same number of months before; the second rollout group compared with the first.
measurement.min_volume: At least two monthly invoicing cycles (about 110 invoices) after the change before the process is credited; the overdue share alone is read as a trend, not proof.
measurement.stop_rule: Pause the firm tier for any client who raises a dispute or hardship until the owner has looked; stop the rollout if two or more clients complain or leave because of the reminders.
